abstract: Let $S$ be the closed subspace of $L^2(0,1)$ of step functions constant on each interval $(1/(m+1),1/m]$. Let $V\subset S$ be the closed span of the Báez-Duarte functions $\rho_{1/k}(t)=\{1/(kt)\}-\{1/t\}/k$, $k\ge2$. By Báez-Duarte's theorem, the Riemann hypothesis holds iff $V=S$. We prove unconditionally that $\dim S/V$ equals the number $|Z^+|$ of zeros of $\zeta$ in $\operatorname{Re}s>1/2$, counted with multiplicity. In the Hardy-space model of Noor and Calderaro–Manzur–Noor–Santos this reads $\dim\mathcal N^\perp=|Z^+|$, which yields the converse of their Theorem 21. The lower bound uses pole orders of $\zeta^{(i)}$ to show that jets at points of $Z^+$ are independent on $S$. For the upper bound when $Z^+$ is finite we adapt Bagchi's proof. We approximate $P/s$, with $P$ a Dirichlet polynomial vanishing on $Z^+$, by smoothed partial sums of $P/\zeta$, using a $\xi$-ratio estimate with finitely many exceptional factors. Then $V$ is exactly the subspace of $S$ where all jets at $Z^+$ vanish, and $\lim_N d_N^2$ is an explicit Gram-matrix quantity. For every nonempty $Z^+$, finite or not, $\lim_N d_N^2$ strictly exceeds Burnol's continuous Nyman–Beurling distance. Unconditionally, a zero $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ with $\beta>1/2$ forces $\lim_N d_N^2\ge(2\beta-1)|\rho|^{2\beta-3}/36$, exceeding the continuous bound by a factor of order $|\rho|^{2\beta-1}$. When $Z^+$ is finite we also prove Burnol-type second-order bounds: $\liminf_N(d_N^2-\lim d_N^2)\log N\ge\sum m(\rho)^2|u(\rho)|^2$ over zeros on the line, where $u$ is the projection of the target onto $V$. The limiting-distance bounds hold, up to a factor $0.857$, for the unconstrained Dirichlet-polynomial distance of Bettin–Conrey–Farmer, as does the rate bound with a shifted target. Spectral synthesis for infinite $Z^+$ remains open. We prove it for $\overline{QS}$ when $|A|\le C|Q|$ on the line for some Dirichlet polynomial $A$ with $c_1(A)\ne0$ and no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>1/2$. Hence $Q$ is cyclic in $S$ iff $c_1(Q)\ne0$ and $Q$ has no such zeros. The general case reduces to one generator $\rho_{1/k}$.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary:
v4 extends §8 (model synthesis for Dirichlet-polynomial multiples). §1–§7 and the main theorems are unchanged.
(1) New Lemma 8.5. Let P be a Dirichlet polynomial with c_1 ≠ 0 and no zeros in Re s > 1/2. (a) Its Bohr symbol has no zeros on any torus T_σ, σ > 1/2 (Kronecker + Hurwitz). (b) The ratio |P(1/2+it)|/|P(1/2+ε+it)| is bounded uniformly in t and 0 < ε ≤ 1, by Weierstrass preparation in the direction (log p)_p.
(2) New Proposition 8.6. If |A| ≤ C|P| on the line for some Dirichlet polynomial A with c_1(A) ≠ 0 and no zeros in Re s > 1/2, then clos(PS) = J_P. It contains Proposition 8.4, since products of positive-real-part polynomials are such A. The torus zero set of P may now have any dimension. v3 needed it finite.
(3) New Corollary 8.7. A Dirichlet polynomial is cyclic in S iff c_1 ≠ 0 and it has no zeros in Re s > 1/2, iff c_1 ≠ 0 and its Bohr symbol has no zeros in the open polydisc. Zeros on the line never obstruct. This is the S-analogue of Neuwirth–Ginsberg–Newman [17] and Nikolski [19], credited as such. The polydisc equivalence uses convexity of amoeba complement components (new refs [22] GKZ, [23] Forsberg–Passare–Tsikh). An example with a torus zero curve is included (code/curve_cyc.py).
(4) The open case is now stated precisely. P× = 1+2√2·2^{-s}+2√3·3^{-s}+√6·6^{-s} has symbol (2+z_2)(z_3−φ(z_2)), with φ a disc automorphism. There is no admissible dominator, by boundary uniqueness on the analytic disc of zeros. Numerically, two necessary tests are consistent with synthesis: single-target upper 0.3041090 vs lower 0.3040650, and eight-target λ_max = 6.85e-4 at M = 10^6. The synthesis question is left open (code/toral_synth.py, code/multi_target.py).
(5) The Scope paragraph and the last sentences of the abstract are updated. One proof step in 8.7 ((ii)⇒(iii), the orthant inclusion) is written out in full. The damping idea in 8.4 remains credited to u/halasz_resonator.
No statement of v3 changed.
title: The Báez-Duarte subspace has codimension equal to the number of zeta zeros off the critical line, with distance and rate bounds not assuming RH
